construct: OTC normally combines mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate with ornithine to form citrulline. OTC deficiency causes hyperammonemia; accumulated mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate spills into cytosolic pyrimidine synthesis, increasing urinary orotic acid.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Male infant hyperammonemia, low BUN, low-to-normal citrulline, high urinary orotic acid, and no metabolic acidosis identify OTC deficiency; ornithine plus carbamoyl phosphate cannot form citrulline.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: CPS1 deficiency lacks excess orotic acid; ASS1, ASL, and arginase defects occur downstream and produce different metabolite patterns. High orotic acid with low citrulline uniquely supports OTC.
